sections.content: How many people stayed in Woking after gaining qualifications?

Woking is a large town in the South East. Woking does not have its own university.

Woking has lower levels of deprivation.

Overall, Woking ended up with:

  • a similar number of graduates as it produced
  • a similar number of non-graduates with advanced qualifications as it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 4,225 state-school pupils from Woking who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 1,790 (42%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 1,290 (31%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Woking to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Woking's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Woking in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Woking move to?

Of Woking's graduates, 560 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 100 of those graduates (18%) were living fairly locally, in the Guildford and Aldershot travel to work area (TTWA).

Of Woking's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 350 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 125 of those qualified non-graduates (36%) were living fairly locally, in the Guildford and Aldershot travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Woking's GCSE cohort:

  • 340 graduates left the South East
  • the most common region they moved to was London
  • 115 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates left the South East
  • the most common region they moved to was London

In 2018 to 2019, 29% of graduates and 23% of qualified non-graduates living in Woking had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 1,685 graduates and 1,190 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Woking. This is compared with the 1,790 graduates and 1,290 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 71% of the graduates had also lived in Woking as GCSE pupils, while 29% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Woking in 2018 to 2019, 77% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 23% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
